For July, keep the visit useful and not rushed:
- Use your car for errands only if needed; it is easy to park and paid for.
- Put the daytime grocery run on the family list so you are not out after dark.
- Ask Daniel and Marco to handle evening grocery runs and any driving-heavy errands.
- Keep one short family outing, one garden check, and one relaxed meal instead of packing every day.
- Leave room for a photo, a card-table visit, and a little yard time, since those matter more than running around.

If you want, I can turn that into a day-by-day schedule.

- Let Kathy arrive with salad and the papers.
- Start with lunch, then do the sorting at the dining table.

- Leave a little crossword or puzzle time after dishes so it does not feel like a workday.
- If the conversation starts drifting into big decisions, steer back to papers, meals, or the family stories that are easy to answer.

That matches the way you already handle Sundays.

For this week, keep it gentle:
- Put the Paducah brochures and the Missouri Star notes together in one folder.
- Spend one short block comparing museum hours, exhibits, and fabric stops.

That will move it forward without turning it into a big project.
